lesson_title: Angle Pairs with Perpendicular, Intersecting and Parallel Lines
hook_text: He measured one wall and cut eight tiles for both. No protractor at the far wall.
clip_script:
A tiler lays a diagonal border across a room whose two long skirting boards are parallel. His apprentice is told to cut the end tiles so the border meets both skirtings cleanly, and reaches for a protractor at the far wall. The tiler stops him: you already measured the near wall; the far wall is the same.

The border meets the near skirting at 50 degrees. On a scrap of board the tiler draws two parallel lines and the slanted border, marks the 50, and finds the letters. An F: corresponding angles, equal, so the far wall's matching angle is 50. A Z: alternate angles, equal, 50 again. A U: co-interior angles, adding to 180. Eight tiles cut, all fitting, from one measurement and three letters.
visual_style: Two parallel skirting lines with a diagonal border; the letters F, Z and U glow over the matching angle pairs in turn as tiles slide into place
call_to_action: Open the full session to name every angle pair and quote the reason that goes with it.
